note: The crash-surviving span journal is an on-disk format, so two SDKs reading the same directory must agree about what it says. Rust declares journal=not_supported in its manifest and skips this file; the day it implements one, these are the cases it has to pass.

journal.name: opens-minus-closes
journal.why: The core rule: a file's unsettled set is its opens minus its closes, in file order.

journal.name: everything-settled
journal.why: A process that exited cleanly leaves nothing to recover, even if its file was never deleted.

journal.name: torn-final-record
journal.why: A SIGKILL mid-write leaves a partial last line. Dropping only the torn record - not the file - is the entire point of one JSON object per line.

journal.name: junk-lines-are-skipped
journal.why: Blank lines, and JSON scalars that parse but are not records, must not become phantom spans.

journal.name: close-without-open
journal.why: A truncated head (the journal is truncated back to empty when nothing is in flight) can leave a close whose open is gone. It must be a no-op, not an error.
